Red-black tree tests for insert, replace, remove, search, traversal, and pool relocation.

# Purpose
This file is a test program for the `fd_redblack.c` red-black tree implementation. It defines a node type, `my_rb_node_t`, and uses the `REDBLK_T` and `REDBLK_NAME` macros to build a tree API for that type. The [`my_rb_compare`](<#my_rb_compare>) function orders nodes by `key`, so the tree stores `key` and `val` pairs and supports ordered search, insert, replace, remove, minimum, maximum, successor, and predecessor operations.

[`main`](<#main>) sets up a fixed-size node pool in aligned scratch memory and then runs a set of tree tests. It checks pool size and footprint rules, inserts nodes in several key orders, verifies search results, tests duplicate-key replacement, walks the tree in sorted order, removes nodes in random order, and verifies tree integrity with `my_rb_verify`. It also copies the backing memory to a second buffer and reattaches the tree with `my_rb_join` to test that node indices remain valid after relocation. The program ends by releasing the tree and pool, deleting the RNG, and printing `pass` if all checks succeed.
